## Hyperparameter Tuning

Peshbeen provides unified hyperparameter tuning via Optuna across all
model families: -
**[`optuna_tune`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/model_selection.html#optuna_tune)**:
For univariate forecasters
([`ml_forecaster`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/02_models/ml_forecast.html#ml_forecaster),
[`ml_direct_forecaster`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/02_models/direct_ml.html#ml_direct_forecaster),
[`arima`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/02_models/arima.html#arima),
[`ets`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/02_models/ets.html#ets),
[`ms_arr`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/02_models/ms_arr.html#ms_arr),
[`glm`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/02_models/glm.html#glm)).
Supports rolling and expanding time-series cross-validation, lag
optimization, Box-Cox variance stabilization, and automated Pareto-based
exogenous feature selection. -
**[`optuna_tune_multi`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/model_selection.html#optuna_tune_multi)**:
For multi-series panel models
([`panel_forecaster`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/02_models/panel_forecast.html#panel_forecaster),
[`ml_multi_forecaster`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/02_models/ml_multi_forecast.html#ml_multi_forecaster)).
Evaluates cross-validation performance across multiple series
simultaneously with options to score on individual or subset target
series.

### Hyperparameter tuning for machine learning models using [`optuna_tune`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/model_selection.html#optuna_tune)

``` python
from peshbeen.datasets import load_airline_passengers
from peshbeen.metrics import MAE, RMSE
from lightgbm import LGBMRegressor
from peshbeen.models import ml_forecaster
from peshbeen.model_selection import optuna_tune

# Load monthly airline passengers dataset
pax = load_airline_passengers()
train = pax[:-12]
test = pax[-12:]

# Create base ML forecaster
ml_model = ml_forecaster(
    model=LGBMRegressor(verbose=-1, random_state=42),
    target_col='passengers',
    lags=12
)
ml_model.fit(train)

# Define hyperparameter search space using Optuna trial suggestions
lgb_param_space = {
    "learning_rate":    lambda t: t.suggest_float("learning_rate", 0.01, 0.3, log=True),
    "num_leaves":       lambda t: t.suggest_int("num_leaves", 10, 50),
    "max_depth":        lambda t: t.suggest_int("max_depth", 2, 8),
    "lags":             lambda t: t.suggest_categorical("lags", [[1, 2, 12], [1, 12], [1, 2, 3, 12]]),
    "box_cox":          lambda t: t.suggest_float("box_cox", 0.0, 2.0),
    "box_cox_biasadj":  lambda t: t.suggest_categorical("box_cox_biasadj", [True, False])
}

# Run cross-validated hyperparameter optimization
best_params, best_lags, other_, _ = optuna_tune(
    model=ml_model,
    df=train,
    cv_split=3,
    step_size=6,
    test_size=12,
    eval_metric=RMSE,
    eval_num=10,
    param_space=lgb_param_space,
    verbose=False
)
print("Best model hyperparameters:", best_params)
print("Best lag structure:", best_lags)
print("Best transformations/box-cox:", other_)
```

    Best model hyperparameters: {'learning_rate': 0.05748924681991978, 'num_leaves': 34, 'max_depth': 2}
    Best lag structure: [1, 2, 12]
    Best transformations/box-cox: {'box_cox': 1.8977710745066665, 'box_cox_biasadj': True}

``` python
# Re-fit a fresh model using the winning parameters and forecast future horizon
final_model = ml_forecaster(
    model=LGBMRegressor(**best_params, verbose=-1, random_state=42),
    target_col='passengers',
    lags=best_lags,
    box_cox=other_.get('box_cox', None),
    box_cox_biasadj=other_.get('box_cox_biasadj', False)
)
final_model.fit(train)
ml_forecasts = final_model.forecast(H=12)
print("Forecasts for next 12 months:", ml_forecasts[:4])
```

    Forecasts for next 12 months: [437.40109234 412.37869871 452.59956269 452.59956269]

### Selecting the best ETS (Error, Trend, Seasonality) model using [`optuna_tune`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/model_selection.html#optuna_tune)

``` python
from peshbeen.models import ets

ets_param_space = {
    "trend":              lambda t: t.suggest_categorical("trend", ["add", "mul", None]),
    "seasonal":           lambda t: t.suggest_categorical("seasonal", ["add", "mul", None]),
    "seasonal_periods":   lambda t: 12,
    "smoothing_level":    lambda t: t.suggest_float("smoothing_level", 0.01, 0.99),
    "smoothing_trend":    lambda t: t.suggest_float("smoothing_trend", 0.01, 0.99),
    "smoothing_seasonal": lambda t: t.suggest_float("smoothing_seasonal", 0.01, 0.99)
}

ets_model = ets(target_col='passengers')
best_params, _, other_, _ = optuna_tune(
    model=ets_model,
    df=train,
    cv_split=3,
    step_size=6,
    test_size=12,
    eval_metric=RMSE,
    eval_num=10,
    param_space=ets_param_space,
    verbose=False
)
print("Best ETS parameters:", best_params)
## add seasonal_periods to the best parameters
best_params["seasonal_periods"] = 12
```

    Best ETS parameters: {'trend': 'add', 'seasonal': 'mul', 'smoothing_level': 0.6216018566289179, 'smoothing_trend': 0.044204810055873955, 'smoothing_seasonal': 0.9825154121511303}

``` python
# Forecast with the best ETS parameters
best_params.update(other_)
tuned_ets = ets(target_col='passengers', **best_params)
tuned_ets.fit(train)
ets_forecasts = tuned_ets.forecast(H=12)
print("ETS forecasts:", ets_forecasts[:4])
```

    ETS forecasts: [431.04450457 400.13769768 474.33078426 455.3642518 ]

``` python
# Evaluate cross-validation performance with best parameters
cv_df = tuned_ets.cross_validate(
    df=train,
    cv_split=3,
    step_size=6,
    test_size=12,
    metrics=[RMSE, MAE]
)
cv_df.head()
```

### Selecting the best orders for an ARIMA model using [`optuna_tune`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/model_selection.html#optuna_tune)

> **Tip:** For automated ARIMA model selection, Peshbeen also provides
> `auto_arima` natively (implementing the Hyndman-Khandakar stepwise
> algorithm and repeated KPSS stationarity tests) with `.top_models()`
> and `.get_orders()`!

``` python
from peshbeen.models import arima

# Search space for SARIMA orders on monthly airline passenger series
candidate_orders = [(1, 1, 1), (0, 1, 1), (1, 1, 0), (2, 1, 1)]
candidate_seasonal = [(1, 1, 1), (0, 1, 1), (1, 1, 0), (0, 1, 0)]

arima_param_space = {
    "order":            lambda t: t.suggest_categorical("order", candidate_orders),
    "seasonal_order":   lambda t: t.suggest_categorical("seasonal_order", candidate_seasonal),
    "seasonal_length":  lambda t: 12,
    "box_cox":          lambda t: t.suggest_float("box_cox", 0.0, 2.0)
}

arima_model = arima(target_col='passengers')
best_params, _, other_, _ = optuna_tune(
    model=arima_model,
    df=train,
    cv_split=3,
    step_size=6,
    test_size=12,
    eval_metric=RMSE,
    eval_num=6,
    param_space=arima_param_space,
    verbose=False
)
print("Best ARIMA orders:", best_params)
best_params["seasonal_periods"] = 12
```

    Best ARIMA orders: {'order': (2, 1, 1), 'seasonal_order': (0, 1, 0)}

### Forward and backward feature selection

Hyperparameter tuning searches over model settings; **feature
selection** searches over *which lags, exogenous columns, and
lag-transforms* to feed the model. peshbeen provides
[`forward_feature_selection`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/model_selection.html#forward_feature_selection)
(start empty, greedily add the candidate that most improves
cross-validation) and
[`backward_feature_selection`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/model_selection.html#backward_feature_selection)
(start from the full set, greedily drop). Both take a *configured but
unfitted*
[`ml_forecaster`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/02_models/ml_forecast.html#ml_forecaster),
the forecast horizon `H`, a list of `metrics` (selection is driven by
the first), and candidate pools via `lags_to_consider`,
`candidate_features`, and `transformations`. Each returns a dict with
`best_lags`, `best_exogs`, and `best_transforms`.

``` python
from peshbeen.model_selection import forward_feature_selection, backward_feature_selection
from peshbeen.metrics import MAE, RMSE
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# Configured-but-unfitted template forecaster
fs_model = ml_forecaster(
    model=LinearRegression(),
    target_col='passengers',
    lags=12,
    difference=1
)

# Forward feature selection over candidate lags 1..12
fwd = forward_feature_selection(
    model=fs_model,
    df=train,
    cv_split=3,
    H=12,
    metric=MAE,
    lags_to_consider=12,
    verbose=False
)
print("Forward-selected features:", fwd)
```

    Forward-selected features: {'best_lags': [], 'best_exogs': [], 'best_transforms': []}

### Hyperparameter tuning for multi-series panel models using [`optuna_tune_multi`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/model_selection.html#optuna_tune_multi)

When optimizing pooled global models
([`panel_forecaster`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/02_models/panel_forecast.html#panel_forecaster)
or
[`ml_multi_forecaster`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/02_models/ml_multi_forecast.html#ml_multi_forecaster)),
[`optuna_tune_multi`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/model_selection.html#optuna_tune_multi)
evaluates time series cross-validation across all series simultaneously.

Key parameters: - `target_series`: Specify a subset of series IDs to
score, which is helpful when tuning models on a representative subset of
critical series. - `transform_back`: When `False`, scores on transformed
scales rather than original units. - `step_size`: Sliding window step
size for fold progression.

``` python
from peshbeen.datasets import load_sales
from peshbeen.models import panel_forecaster
from peshbeen.model_selection import optuna_tune_multi
from peshbeen.metrics import RMSE
from lightgbm import LGBMRegressor

# Load multi-series sales and filter to a small subset for demonstration
sales_data = load_sales()
subset_items = ['store_01_item_01', 'store_01_item_02']
df_panel = sales_data[sales_data['store_item'].isin(subset_items)].groupby('store_item').tail(120)

# Base panel model
panel_model = panel_forecaster(
    model=LGBMRegressor(verbose=-1, random_state=42),
    id_col='store_item',
    target_col='sales',
    lags=7
)

# Search space for panel model hyperparameters and pooled lag length
panel_space = {
    "learning_rate": lambda t: t.suggest_float("learning_rate", 0.02, 0.2),
    "num_leaves":    lambda t: t.suggest_int("num_leaves", 10, 40),
    "lags":          lambda t: t.suggest_categorical("lags", [[1, 2, 7], [1, 7], [1, 2, 3, 7]])
}

best_panel_h, best_panel_lags, other_panel = optuna_tune_multi(
    model=panel_model,
    df=df_panel,
    cv_split=3,
    test_size=14,
    eval_metric=RMSE,
    param_space=panel_space,
    eval_num=5,
    verbose=False
)
print("Best panel parameters:", best_panel_h)
print("Best panel lags:", best_panel_lags)
```

    Best panel parameters: {'learning_rate': 0.023705208973244442, 'num_leaves': 40}
    Best panel lags: [1, 2, 7]

### The metrics module

All tuning and selection functions accept any metric from
`peshbeen.metrics`. Most are **two-argument** functions
`metric(y_true, y_pred)`:

- [`MAPE`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/metrics.html#mape),
  [`SMAPE`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/metrics.html#smape),
  [`WMAPE`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/metrics.html#wmape)
  — percentage errors
- [`MAE`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/metrics.html#mae),
  [`MSE`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/metrics.html#mse),
  [`RMSE`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/metrics.html#rmse)
  — absolute / squared errors
- [`CFE`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/metrics.html#cfe),
  [`CFE_ABS`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/metrics.html#cfe_abs)
  — cumulative forecast error (bias) and its absolute value

The **scaled** metrics are *three-argument* —
`metric(y_true, y_pred, y_train)` — because they normalise the error by
the in-sample scale of the training series:

- [`MASE`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/metrics.html#mase)
  — mean absolute scaled error
- [`RMSSE`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/metrics.html#rmsse)
  — root mean squared scaled error
- [`SRMSE`](https://mustafaslanCoto.github.io/peshbeen/modules/metrics.html#srmse)
  — scaled RMSE

When you call a scaled metric directly you must pass the training target
as the third argument; for example
`MASE(y_true, y_pred, y_train=train['admissions'])`.
